description: Interactive map with tile, UDF and SQL layers.

basemap.description: Mapbox style URL (e.g. "mapbox://styles/mapbox/dark-v11", "mapbox://styles/mapbox/light-v11", "mapbox://styles/mapbox/satellite-streets-v12") or "blank" for a plain background. Omit it so the map follows the app light/dark theme; when the viewer picks a basemap in the switcher it is written into this prop, so only set it when a fixed basemap is wanted.

basemapGroups.description: The basemap's own feature groups: "label" (place, road and POI names, icons, shields), "road", "border", "building", "water", "land". Can be set from the Base map tab.

aboveData.description: Base map groups drawn above the data layers instead of under them. ["label"] keeps names readable over filled polygons, hexagons and rasters. Groups keep the basemap's own order among themselves.

hidden.description: Base map groups not drawn at all, e.g. ["road", "building"] for a quieter basemap.

layerBlending.description: How the data layers blend where they overlap, one setting for every layer (kepler.gl's Layer blending, same values): "normal" (the default, plain alpha), "additive" (overlaps grow brighter; reads best on a dark basemap) or "subtractive" (overlaps grow darker). Layers draw into the basemap, so the blend mixes with its pixels too. The selection outline and failed-tile squares stay normal, and raster layers stay normal under subtractive (their transparent pixels would black out the basemap). Picking it in the sidebar's Layers tab writes it here; normal removes it.

centerLng.description: Map centre longitude (defaults to -98). Setting centerLng or centerLat turns auto-fit off unless autoFit is set explicitly, and the map opens at centerLng/centerLat/zoom on every load or refresh instead of the camera the viewer left behind.

centerLat.description: Map centre latitude (defaults to 39.5). Setting centerLng or centerLat turns auto-fit off unless autoFit is set explicitly, and the map opens at centerLng/centerLat/zoom on every load or refresh instead of the camera the viewer left behind.

zoom.description: Initial zoom level; only used when auto-fit is off.

autoFit.description: Fly to the loaded data once on first load: inline GeoJSON plus every visible udf / sql row layer. Defaults to true, or false when centerLng/centerLat is set (an explicit camera wins). Later pans, re-runs and basemap switches leave the camera alone, and a camera the viewer left behind wins unless the config sets centerLng/centerLat. Tile layers never report bounds. When off the map opens at centerLng/centerLat/zoom.

type.description: Layer type. Omit it to detect from the data: an image → raster (tiles from a tile UDF, else one image placed at the bounds the run returned or was sent), an H3 cell column → h3, start/end lat-lng pairs → arc, one lat-lng pair → scatterplot, a geometry column → geojson. The detected type and columns are written into this config once known. geojson: polygons/lines/points from inline data, sql or udf rows (deck-geojson is an alias of geojson; prefer geojson). h3: hexagons from h3Column. scatterplot: point circles. heatmap: point density. arc: source→target arcs. raster: tiles from tileUrl or a udf with tile: true, else a single image from a udf. mvt: tiles from tileUrl, or from udf with tile: true. fused-hex: H3 tiles queried from a Fused server's ERA5, gridMET or /h3/query endpoints (see source); it is never detected, so set it explicitly. For your own data: partition it with fused.h3.partition, register it with fused.h3.index, then set source {path, overview: {}} and h3Column. Row tiles load from the layer's zoom floor (default zoom 7) and a zoomed-out overview of the whole dataset draws below it. fused-bbox: features of a dataset indexed by bounding box (fused.bbox.index, for tables written by fused.ingest or GeoParquet with a bbox covering), queried per tile from /bbox/query; never detected either. Set source {path, overview: {}}; its rows draw as geojson from the zoom floor (minZoom, default 8) and the boxes of its chunks draw below it. composite: one layer made of several layers (`levels`, each any other layer type), each bound to a map zoom range, for level of detail (coarse aggregates zoomed out, fine cells or shapes zoomed in); it hands over between levels without the map flashing empty. Set levels (and h3Column for fused-hex levels); never detected.

tileUrl.description: Tile URL template with {x}/{y}/{z} placeholders (mvt, raster, tiled h3)

minZoom.description: Tiled layers only (tileUrl, a udf with tile: true, fused-hex, fused-bbox): the lowest zoom of the layer's data. While the tile zoom is below it no tiles are requested or drawn, so a wide view does not fire thousands of requests. Ignored by non-tiled layers. To hide a layer by zoom without changing what it loads, use visibleMinZoom.

maxZoom.description: Tiled layers only: the highest zoom of the layer's data. Zoomed in past it, no deeper tiles are requested and the maxZoom tiles keep drawing, enlarged (over-zoomed); the layer does not disappear. Set it to the deepest zoom your tiles differ at to save requests. To hide a layer past a zoom, use visibleMaxZoom. On a composite: the deepest tile zoom of every tiled level (each level's tiles also stop at its own maxZoom, which ends its band); a layer turned into a composite keeps its maxZoom there.

visibleMinZoom.description: Hides the layer while the map zoom is below this; it shows at exactly this zoom and above. Any layer type. Only the drawing stops: the layer's data, loaded tiles and runs are kept, so it reappears without a refetch. Not the same as minZoom, which is the lowest zoom a tiled layer's data exists at. Omit for no lower limit. Example: 10 shows a detailed layer only once the viewer zooms in to 10.

visibleMaxZoom.description: Hides the layer while the map zoom is above this; it shows at exactly this zoom and below. Any layer type. Only the drawing stops: the layer's data, loaded tiles and runs are kept, so it reappears without a refetch. Not the same as maxZoom, past which a tiled layer keeps drawing its maxZoom tiles enlarged. Omit for no upper limit. Example: 12 hides a zoomed-out summary layer once the viewer zooms past 12.

zoomOffset.description: Tiled layers only: an integer added to the zoom tiles are requested at. 1 requests tiles one level finer than the map zoom (four times as many, more detail); -1 one level coarser (a quarter as many, useful to generalize H3 tiles). minZoom and maxZoom bound the offset zoom.

maxRequests.description: Maximum parallel tile requests for tiled layers. 0 means no limit.

autoRetry.description: Retry failed tiles automatically: a few fetch attempts on transient errors, and a refetch when a failed tile scrolls back into view. Default true. Set false to make a tile fail after one attempt and stay failed until Retry.

bounds.description: Lock a udf tile layer (tile: true) drawn as geojson or deck-geojson to these bounds [minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]: the UDF runs once with bounds passed as a parameter (a JSON string "[w, s, e, n]", like the legacy single-viewport run) and the result renders as one static layer, with no per-tile runs and no refetch on pan or zoom. A sql on the layer runs on that one result while locked, and over the tiles in view otherwise. Ignored by other layers: other types (h3, scatterplot, arc, heatmap, raster, mvt) keep their tiles.

sourceLayer.description: Source layer name for MVT tiles (defaults to 'default')

data.description: Inline GeoJSON FeatureCollection, or one {{name}} placeholder naming a canvas SQL source: an h3-query or sql-runner widget's name (offered by Add layer and wired by an edge automatically), or another map's layer id (draw the edge from that map yourself). The source's rows are read from DuckDB as they are (no UDF runs; its loading and errors show on the layer; it re-queries when the widget fetches again), and the edge from that node to this one grants access, as for a UDF. Add sql to query them ({{source}} or {{name}} reads the rows). Row layers only (geojson, h3, scatterplot, heatmap, arc, or type omitted to detect from the rows): not with tile, udf or tileUrl, nor on raster, mvt or fused-hex. Example: "{{h3_rows}}" with h3Column "hex".

udf.description: UDF placeholder, e.g. {{my_udf}}, {{my_udf?param=value}} or {{my_udf?param=$param_name}}. The UDF is run directly (no share token needed) and re-run when it or a referenced $param_name changes: the whole result as rows for geojson and deck-geojson layers, or per tile when tile is true (a sql then queries the tiles in view). An input in the same widget (slider, number-input, with a defaultValue) can drive it; only the UDF → widget edge is needed. Combine with sql to query the result (the tiles in view when tile is true). Mutually exclusive with tileUrl.

tile.description: With udf: run the UDF per XYZ tile (raster → PNG bitmaps, h3 → hexagons, geojson → vector features). Required when type is mvt and the source is a udf. Without it a raster udf layer runs once and draws one image at the bounds the run returned (`image, bounds`) or was sent (the map view at the time of the run, for a UDF with a bounds parameter; moving the map later does not run it again). Tiled layers never auto-fit and ignore the whole-result size limit.

sql.description: DuckDB SQL query with {{name}} placeholders: a UDF result, or a canvas SQL source (an h3-query or sql-runner widget's name, another map's layer id) read from DuckDB with no UDF run. Rows are converted to GeoJSON for rendering. On a tiled layer (udf with tile: true, or fused-hex) the query runs once over the rows of every tile loaded in the current view, reading them as {{source}}, which takes no ?params (a udf layer may also write its own {{udf_name}}, bare or with exactly its own ?params), and runs again as the view moves (pan, zoom), the query changes or a $param changes; no tile is refetched. WHERE, computed columns, GROUP BY, aggregates, LIMIT, ORDER BY and USING SAMPLE apply to the whole view (before a fused-hex reduce); only a single SELECT (a WITH is fine) over {{source}} runs (no UNION, several statements, other UDFs or joins), and its result must keep the cell column (h3, fused-hex) or the geometry columns (vector layers). raster, mvt and tileUrl layers take no sql.

filters.description: Feature filters applied on the client: range filters on numeric properties, category filters on any property.

min.description: Inclusive lower bound, or a `$param` holding one

anyOf.description: A canvas parameter reference such as `$day_min`; the filter reads its value live and is inactive while the parameter has none

max.description: Inclusive upper bound, or a `$param` holding one

anyOf.description: A canvas parameter reference such as `$day_min`; the filter reads its value live and is inactive while the parameter has none
A canvas parameter reference such as `$day_min`; the filter reads its value live and is inactive while the parameter has none

values.description: Values to keep (empty keeps every feature), or a `$param` holding the list

attr.description: Feature property holding each row's time: ISO date or datetime text (no zone reads as UTC), other common date text, or an epoch number in seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds (told apart by size)

min.description: Inclusive start of the time window: ISO date or datetime, epoch milliseconds, or a `$param` holding either

max.description: Inclusive end of the time window: ISO date or datetime, epoch milliseconds, or a `$param` holding either

playback.description: Open the map's time playback bar on this filter when the map loads. The bar plays one filter at a time; its clock button sets and clears this

playbackOptions.description: The playback bar's settings for this filter, kept while the bar is closed. Every key is optional; one at its default is left out

mode.description: How the playback bar plays: auto (default: a click on the chart shows one bar, a drag a window), window (a window of fixed width moves), point (one histogram bar at a time), cumulative (the start pinned on the first time, the end grows)

skipEmpty.description: Play jumps over stretches with no rows instead of crossing them at one pace (default false). Point mode always skips

interval.description: One histogram bar's length as `<step>-<unit>`, unit one of millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, year (`1-day`, `15-minute`), aligned on the calendar of `timezone`; also what one point plays. Absent: 100 equal bars over the data's time range

timezone.description: IANA time zone the bar prints times and aligns intervals in (`Europe/Paris`); default UTC

timeFormat.description: Clock the bar prints times with; default 24-hour

yAxis.description: The playback chart's y axis; absent, it counts rows

field.description: Numeric property the chart plots per bar instead of the row count

aggregation.description: How the field's values in one bar combine; default average

fit.description: Fit the y range to the values instead of starting at 0 (default false)

collapsed.description: The playback bar shows as one slim row, without its chart (default false); the chevron on the bar sets and clears this

speed.description: Speed multiplier play runs at, any number above 0 (default 1)

geometryColumn.description: Column containing the geometry: GeoJSON strings (use ST_AsGeoJSON in SQL), GeoJSON objects, or WKB blobs as stored by GeoDataFrame outputs. Defaults to 'geometry'.

h3Column.description: Column containing H3 hex indexes (h3 layer type). Auto-detected from common names (hex, h3, ...) when omitted.

latColumn.description: Column for latitude (point data). Defaults to 'lat'.

lngColumn.description: Column for longitude (point data). Defaults to 'lng'.

startLatColumn.description: Column for the arc start latitude (arc layer type).

startLngColumn.description: Column for the arc start longitude (arc layer type).

endLatColumn.description: Column for the arc end latitude (arc layer type).

endLngColumn.description: Column for the arc end longitude (arc layer type).

tooltip.description: Show tooltip on hover. true = all properties, string[] = specific properties. Off for data rows when unset. A fused-hex overview cell always shows its hover (cell, rows, rows in window) unless this is false.

legend.description: Show color legend for this layer. true = auto title (the layer's name), {title} = custom title; unset or false: none. It shows fillColor's scale when fillColor is data-driven, else lineColor's when fillColor is unset and lineColor is data-driven; a single-colour fillColor shows none.

source.description: fused-hex and fused-bbox. fused-bbox reads only path, overview {minZoom, extent}, variables (columns to fetch; all when unset) and maxRowGroups, e.g. {path: 's3://bucket/table/', overview: {}}. fused-hex: the server endpoint and query each XYZ tile's bbox is sent to. For your own data, set path to an indexed folder and overview to {}; the layer then also needs h3Column. Example: {path: 's3://bucket/indexed/', overview: {}} with h3Column 'hex' and style.fillColor {type: 'continuous', attr: 'temp'}. composite: optional source options shared by every level that reads a source (variables, loader, timeColumn, reduce, limit, ...), merged under each level's own source; path and endpoint here are never inherited (always the level's own), though they make a level without a type a fused-hex level. overview is not drawn by a composite (a layer turned into one keeps it here, so turning it back restores it).

endpoint.description: Bbox query endpoint on a Fused server: a full URL or a path relative to the current server root. Supported: /retrieve/era5/daily/bbox, /retrieve/era5/hourly/bbox, /retrieve/gridmet/bbox and /h3/query. Defaults to /h3/query when path is set.

path.description: Indexed dataset location, e.g. s3://bucket/indexed/data/. Sets the endpoint to /h3/query when none is given. Needs the layer's h3Column (the location's indexed space column, 'hex' for what fused.h3.partition writes). The folder must be hex-sorted H3 parquet that fused.h3.partition wrote and fused.h3.index registered for your team (run partition, then index; pass chunk_res_offset to partition for the chunk-level overview). Not used by the retrieve endpoints, which serve a fixed dataset.

dateMin.description: Inclusive start of the time window (ISO date or datetime). Required for the retrieve endpoints.

dateMax.description: Inclusive end of the time window (ISO date or datetime). Required for the retrieve endpoints.

variables.description: Measurement columns to fetch. Defaults to the attributes the style, tooltip and filters name, or every column when none do.

reduce.description: How each hex's rows across the time window collapse to one value: latest (default) or first keep one time step; mean, min, max and sum aggregate every numeric variable and add count, date_min and date_max. Ignored while the layer's time filter on its time column holds one instant (time playback, experimental): the layer then draws that time step.

hour.description: Hourly datasets only: keep rows for this hour of the day before reducing.

timeColumn.description: Column holding each row's time, used to order rows for latest/first and, with time playback (experimental), the column a time filter plays the layer's time steps on. Defaults to 'date' for the retrieve endpoints; set it for /h3/query datasets.

limit.description: Server row cap per tile request (the endpoint's `limit`)

maxRowGroups.description: Server row group cap per tile request (`max_row_groups`)

maxRanges.description: Retrieve endpoints only: cell ranges the bbox cover may use (`max_ranges`). Higher values cover each tile more tightly, so fewer rows outside it are read.

minZoom.description: The overview needs the layer's zoom floor above this (default 3). It draws at every zoom below the floor, where row tiles start.

extent.description: [west, south, east, north] the overview looks up files in, with west < east (boxes crossing the antimeridian are not supported). Row tiles are also confined to it: none are requested outside it. Cells are drawn only inside it, in the overview and in rows, by cell centre. Defaults to the whole world.

overview.description: Zoomed-out view below the layer's zoom floor, drawn from one request, so `overview: {}` is all it takes. Each cell is a file's H3 cell (file level) or, when the location was partitioned chunk-aligned (fused.h3.partition with chunk_res_offset) and has at most 100,000 distinct chunk cells, one row-group chunk (chunk level). The server picks the level; ERA5 and gridMET are always file level. Default at both levels: cells fill light by row count with grey outlines, not coloured by the layer's colour. Cells carry only their row counts, never column values, at either level. Hovering a cell shows it, its row count and the rows the current date window reads. Available for the ERA5 and gridMET retrieve endpoints and /h3/query. style.overview overrides the colours.

loader.description: How each tile's row groups are read. server (the default) has the server read them and answer Parquet pages. browser reads the row groups from object storage in the browser, from a plan the server answers (/h3/query with format=browser); it needs an execution environment, and a share link without one fails. auto tries browser and falls back to server when the plan is refused or the browser loader cannot start. reader sends the query to the regional reader service (fast path for read-only Parquet pages) when the client is configured with one, and falls back to server when it is not configured or refuses the request.

maxChunks.description: Browser and auto loaders only: most chunks (storage range requests) the browser may fetch for one tile page. Defaults to 1000. A tile whose plan needs more is not loaded and the layer shows a warning naming the value to set here.

fillColor.description: Fill color (source colour for arc, weight attr for heatmap): [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a] array, CSS string, or data-driven {type:"continuous", attr, domain?:[min,max], palette?, steps?, reverse?, nullColor?, scaleType?:"quantize"|"quantile"} | {type:"categorical", attr, colors?:{value:"#hex"}, palette?, nullColor?}. See the component description for palette names.

lineColor.description: Stroke color (target colour for arc): [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a] array, CSS string, or the same data-driven {type:"continuous"|"categorical", attr, ...} object as fillColor. Shapes, hexagons and points draw no outline by default: setting lineColor or lineWidth turns it on.

lineWidth.description: Stroke width in pixels. Shapes, hexagons and points draw no outline unless lineColor or lineWidth is set; 0 turns a configured outline off. Line features of a geojson layer always draw.

minPixels.description: Smallest width on screen, in pixels, of a polygon or an H3 cell. A shape keeps its real geometry until it would draw smaller, then stays this wide about its own centre (and may overlap its neighbours), so it still shows zoomed all the way out, as a stroke and a point do. Defaults to 2; 0 lets shapes shrink with the map. Not applied to extruded shapes.

coverage.description: H3 hex coverage 0-1 (1 = no gap, 0.8 = small gaps). Defaults to 1 for fused-hex layers, 0.9 for other hex layers.

coverageAttr.description: Hex layers (h3, fused-hex): numeric column that sizes each cell. Its value is mapped from coverageDomain onto a size factor in coverageRange, and the cell draws at coverage times that factor, so coverage stays the largest size. A cell with no value draws at the low end. Unset: every cell draws at coverage.

coverageDomain.description: Values of coverageAttr mapped from, [low, high]: low draws at coverageRange[0], high at coverageRange[1], values between scale linearly and values outside clamp to the nearer end. Defaults to [0, 1], so set it to the column's range (e.g. [0, 500]).

coverageRange.description: Size factors 0-1 that coverageDomain maps to, [low, high], each times coverage. Defaults to [0, 1]; [0.2, 1] keeps the smallest cells visible.

elevationAttr.description: Feature property to use for extrusion height

overview.description: fused-hex only, optional: overrides how the overview cells (source.overview) draw; leave it out for the defaults, which need no setting. Defaults, at both levels: light fill by row count with #afafaf outlines at opacity 0.35, not coloured by the layer's colour. Cells carry only row counts (row_count_total, row_count_window), so a colour can only be data-driven by those; hovering a cell shows it and its row counts. Example: {fillColor: [255, 140, 0], opacity: 0.5, lineWidth: 0}. null clears a configured block (a layer switched out of fused-hex).

fillColor.description: Unset or "auto": a light fill by row_count_total at both levels, so the overview does not read as data coloured by a column. A single colour fills the cells; null draws no fill; "inherit" takes the layer's fillColor (a single colour is used as is; a data-driven one falls back to the row-count fill, since cells carry no column values); or a data-driven {type:"continuous"|"categorical", attr, ...} over the only cell properties: row_count_total (rows in the cell's files or chunk) and row_count_window (rows the current date window reads). Any other attr falls back to the row-count fill.

opacity.description: Opacity 0-1 of the overview cells, fill and outline alike. Defaults to 0.35; with fillColor "inherit" of a single colour at the chunk level, the layer's own opacity.

lineColor.description: Unset or "auto": #afafaf at both levels. A single colour outlines the cells; "inherit" takes the layer's lineColor (a data-driven one falls back to #afafaf); or a data-driven {type:"continuous"|"categorical", attr, ...} over the same cell properties as fillColor.

lineWidth.description: Overview cell stroke width in pixels. Defaults to 1 at both levels; 0 draws no outline.

stat.description: No longer used and ignored: overview cells carry no column statistics. Accepted so saved configs that set it still load.

levels.description: composite only, required there: the levels, each an ordinary layer (any type but composite) bound to a map zoom range. Exactly one level draws at a time, the one whose [minZoom, maxZoom) holds the map zoom (where ranges overlap, the one with the highest minZoom; a zoom no level covers draws nothing). A level without a data source yet, or a fused-hex level with a path but no h3Column, draws nothing and is no error while another level draws: the level below it, where their ranges touch, draws over its range. Crossing into another level keeps the previous level drawing until the new level has loaded the view (a tiled level: its tiles in view; a row level: its rows), then they swap in one frame, so the map never flashes empty. A level is read and drawn exactly as a layer of its type: it may set any layer key (type, source, udf, tile, data, sql, tileUrl, sourceLayer, filters, h3Column, latColumn, geometryColumn, tooltip, legend, style, zoomOffset, maxRequests, autoRetry, ...). The composite holds the defaults and a level stores only what differs: objects (style, source, legend) merge key by key over the composite's, a fillColor or lineColor replaces the composite's whole, arrays (tooltip) and plain values (udf, type, ...) replace, null unsets the composite's value at that level. Data: a level takes each of the composite's udf, data and tileUrl it does not set itself (null unsets that one only), except what cannot stand next to its own: a level reading its own source path or endpoint takes none, one with its own {{name}} data takes no udf or tileUrl, one with its own udf or tileUrl takes no data (a level's own udf next to the composite's tileUrl draws the tile URL, as a layer with both does; tileUrl: null there unsets it). sql and filters STACK instead: the composite's query and filters apply at every level, always; a level's own sql runs first and the composite's sql over its result (one query), and a row must pass the level's filters and the composite's (null or unset on a level adds nothing). The composite's `source` holds options shared by every source level (variables, loader, timeColumn, reduce, limit, ...); path and endpoint are always the level's own. A level without a type is fused-hex when it (or the composite) names a source path or endpoint, else detected from its data. visible, visibleMinZoom and visibleMaxZoom are the composite's only (a level's are ignored). A level's `id` is its own key within the composite, not a layer id: give each level an `id` (e.g. "z4") so editing the list keeps the right level on screen. Each level keeps its own colour scale. A composite filter on a column a level does not fetch (not in its source.variables, or absent from its rows) is skipped at that level; a level's own filters always apply. Example: [{id: "z0", maxZoom: 6, source: {path: "s3://b/res5/"}}, {id: "z6", minZoom: 6, maxZoom: 10, type: "scatterplot", data: "{{points}}", sql: "SELECT * FROM {{points}} WHERE pop > 1000"}, {id: "z10", minZoom: 10, type: "geojson", udf: "{{buildings}}", tile: true, tooltip: ["name"]}].

anyOf.description: Tile URL template with {x}/{y}/{z} placeholders (mvt, raster, tiled h3)

tileUrl.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Tile URL template with {x}/{y}/{z} placeholders (mvt, raster, tiled h3)

anyOf.description: Tiled layers only: an integer added to the zoom tiles are requested at. 1 requests tiles one level finer than the map zoom (four times as many, more detail); -1 one level coarser (a quarter as many, useful to generalize H3 tiles). minZoom and maxZoom bound the offset zoom.

zoomOffset.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Tiled layers only: an integer added to the zoom tiles are requested at. 1 requests tiles one level finer than the map zoom (four times as many, more detail); -1 one level coarser (a quarter as many, useful to generalize H3 tiles). minZoom and maxZoom bound the offset zoom.

anyOf.description: Maximum parallel tile requests for tiled layers. 0 means no limit.

maxRequests.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Maximum parallel tile requests for tiled layers. 0 means no limit.

anyOf.description: Retry failed tiles automatically: a few fetch attempts on transient errors, and a refetch when a failed tile scrolls back into view. Default true. Set false to make a tile fail after one attempt and stay failed until Retry.

autoRetry.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Retry failed tiles automatically: a few fetch attempts on transient errors, and a refetch when a failed tile scrolls back into view. Default true. Set false to make a tile fail after one attempt and stay failed until Retry.

anyOf.description: Lock a udf tile layer (tile: true) drawn as geojson or deck-geojson to these bounds [minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]: the UDF runs once with bounds passed as a parameter (a JSON string "[w, s, e, n]", like the legacy single-viewport run) and the result renders as one static layer, with no per-tile runs and no refetch on pan or zoom. A sql on the layer runs on that one result while locked, and over the tiles in view otherwise. Ignored by other layers: other types (h3, scatterplot, arc, heatmap, raster, mvt) keep their tiles.

bounds.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Lock a udf tile layer (tile: true) drawn as geojson or deck-geojson to these bounds [minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]: the UDF runs once with bounds passed as a parameter (a JSON string "[w, s, e, n]", like the legacy single-viewport run) and the result renders as one static layer, with no per-tile runs and no refetch on pan or zoom. A sql on the layer runs on that one result while locked, and over the tiles in view otherwise. Ignored by other layers: other types (h3, scatterplot, arc, heatmap, raster, mvt) keep their tiles.

anyOf.description: Source layer name for MVT tiles (defaults to 'default')

sourceLayer.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Source layer name for MVT tiles (defaults to 'default')

anyOf.description: Inline GeoJSON FeatureCollection, or one {{name}} placeholder naming a canvas SQL source: an h3-query or sql-runner widget's name (offered by Add layer and wired by an edge automatically), or another map's layer id (draw the edge from that map yourself). The source's rows are read from DuckDB as they are (no UDF runs; its loading and errors show on the layer; it re-queries when the widget fetches again), and the edge from that node to this one grants access, as for a UDF. Add sql to query them ({{source}} or {{name}} reads the rows). Row layers only (geojson, h3, scatterplot, heatmap, arc, or type omitted to detect from the rows): not with tile, udf or tileUrl, nor on raster, mvt or fused-hex. Example: "{{h3_rows}}" with h3Column "hex".

data.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Inline GeoJSON FeatureCollection, or one {{name}} placeholder naming a canvas SQL source: an h3-query or sql-runner widget's name (offered by Add layer and wired by an edge automatically), or another map's layer id (draw the edge from that map yourself). The source's rows are read from DuckDB as they are (no UDF runs; its loading and errors show on the layer; it re-queries when the widget fetches again), and the edge from that node to this one grants access, as for a UDF. Add sql to query them ({{source}} or {{name}} reads the rows). Row layers only (geojson, h3, scatterplot, heatmap, arc, or type omitted to detect from the rows): not with tile, udf or tileUrl, nor on raster, mvt or fused-hex. Example: "{{h3_rows}}" with h3Column "hex".

anyOf.description: UDF placeholder, e.g. {{my_udf}}, {{my_udf?param=value}} or {{my_udf?param=$param_name}}. The UDF is run directly (no share token needed) and re-run when it or a referenced $param_name changes: the whole result as rows for geojson and deck-geojson layers, or per tile when tile is true (a sql then queries the tiles in view). An input in the same widget (slider, number-input, with a defaultValue) can drive it; only the UDF → widget edge is needed. Combine with sql to query the result (the tiles in view when tile is true). Mutually exclusive with tileUrl.

udf.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). UDF placeholder, e.g. {{my_udf}}, {{my_udf?param=value}} or {{my_udf?param=$param_name}}. The UDF is run directly (no share token needed) and re-run when it or a referenced $param_name changes: the whole result as rows for geojson and deck-geojson layers, or per tile when tile is true (a sql then queries the tiles in view). An input in the same widget (slider, number-input, with a defaultValue) can drive it; only the UDF → widget edge is needed. Combine with sql to query the result (the tiles in view when tile is true). Mutually exclusive with tileUrl.

anyOf.description: With udf: run the UDF per XYZ tile (raster → PNG bitmaps, h3 → hexagons, geojson → vector features). Required when type is mvt and the source is a udf. Without it a raster udf layer runs once and draws one image at the bounds the run returned (`image, bounds`) or was sent (the map view at the time of the run, for a UDF with a bounds parameter; moving the map later does not run it again). Tiled layers never auto-fit and ignore the whole-result size limit.

tile.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). With udf: run the UDF per XYZ tile (raster → PNG bitmaps, h3 → hexagons, geojson → vector features). Required when type is mvt and the source is a udf. Without it a raster udf layer runs once and draws one image at the bounds the run returned (`image, bounds`) or was sent (the map view at the time of the run, for a UDF with a bounds parameter; moving the map later does not run it again). Tiled layers never auto-fit and ignore the whole-result size limit.

anyOf.description: DuckDB SQL query with {{name}} placeholders: a UDF result, or a canvas SQL source (an h3-query or sql-runner widget's name, another map's layer id) read from DuckDB with no UDF run. Rows are converted to GeoJSON for rendering. On a tiled layer (udf with tile: true, or fused-hex) the query runs once over the rows of every tile loaded in the current view, reading them as {{source}}, which takes no ?params (a udf layer may also write its own {{udf_name}}, bare or with exactly its own ?params), and runs again as the view moves (pan, zoom), the query changes or a $param changes; no tile is refetched. WHERE, computed columns, GROUP BY, aggregates, LIMIT, ORDER BY and USING SAMPLE apply to the whole view (before a fused-hex reduce); only a single SELECT (a WITH is fine) over {{source}} runs (no UNION, several statements, other UDFs or joins), and its result must keep the cell column (h3, fused-hex) or the geometry columns (vector layers). raster, mvt and tileUrl layers take no sql.

sql.description: The level's own DuckDB query, ADDED to the composite's (never replacing it): it runs first, over the level's own rows ({{source}}: its tiles in view, its udf result, or its data source), and the composite's sql then runs over its result (the composite's {{source}} reads this query's rows), as one query. Write here what only this level needs (reshape its data, e.g. cell centres as lat/lng for a scatterplot level); write what every level needs on the composite. null or unset: the level adds no query (the composite's still runs). If the composite's query fails at this level (e.g. it names a column the level lacks), the level draws this query's rows and the error names the composite's query.

anyOf.description: Feature filters applied on the client: range filters on numeric properties, category filters on any property.

min.description: Inclusive lower bound, or a `$param` holding one

anyOf.description: A canvas parameter reference such as `$day_min`; the filter reads its value live and is inactive while the parameter has none

max.description: Inclusive upper bound, or a `$param` holding one

anyOf.description: A canvas parameter reference such as `$day_min`; the filter reads its value live and is inactive while the parameter has none
A canvas parameter reference such as `$day_min`; the filter reads its value live and is inactive while the parameter has none

values.description: Values to keep (empty keeps every feature), or a `$param` holding the list

attr.description: Feature property holding each row's time: ISO date or datetime text (no zone reads as UTC), other common date text, or an epoch number in seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds (told apart by size)

min.description: Inclusive start of the time window: ISO date or datetime, epoch milliseconds, or a `$param` holding either

max.description: Inclusive end of the time window: ISO date or datetime, epoch milliseconds, or a `$param` holding either

playback.description: Open the map's time playback bar on this filter when the map loads. The bar plays one filter at a time; its clock button sets and clears this

playbackOptions.description: The playback bar's settings for this filter, kept while the bar is closed. Every key is optional; one at its default is left out

mode.description: How the playback bar plays: auto (default: a click on the chart shows one bar, a drag a window), window (a window of fixed width moves), point (one histogram bar at a time), cumulative (the start pinned on the first time, the end grows)

skipEmpty.description: Play jumps over stretches with no rows instead of crossing them at one pace (default false). Point mode always skips

interval.description: One histogram bar's length as `<step>-<unit>`, unit one of millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, year (`1-day`, `15-minute`), aligned on the calendar of `timezone`; also what one point plays. Absent: 100 equal bars over the data's time range

timezone.description: IANA time zone the bar prints times and aligns intervals in (`Europe/Paris`); default UTC

timeFormat.description: Clock the bar prints times with; default 24-hour

yAxis.description: The playback chart's y axis; absent, it counts rows

field.description: Numeric property the chart plots per bar instead of the row count

aggregation.description: How the field's values in one bar combine; default average

fit.description: Fit the y range to the values instead of starting at 0 (default false)

collapsed.description: The playback bar shows as one slim row, without its chart (default false); the chevron on the bar sets and clears this

speed.description: Speed multiplier play runs at, any number above 0 (default 1)

filters.description: The level's own feature filters, ADDED to the composite's: a row draws only when it passes both. null or unset: none of its own (the composite's still apply). Unlike the composite's filters, which are skipped at a level whose rows lack their column, a level's own filter always applies.

anyOf.description: Column containing the geometry: GeoJSON strings (use ST_AsGeoJSON in SQL), GeoJSON objects, or WKB blobs as stored by GeoDataFrame outputs. Defaults to 'geometry'.

geometryColumn.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Column containing the geometry: GeoJSON strings (use ST_AsGeoJSON in SQL), GeoJSON objects, or WKB blobs as stored by GeoDataFrame outputs. Defaults to 'geometry'.

anyOf.description: Column containing H3 hex indexes (h3 layer type). Auto-detected from common names (hex, h3, ...) when omitted.

h3Column.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Column containing H3 hex indexes (h3 layer type). Auto-detected from common names (hex, h3, ...) when omitted.

anyOf.description: Column for latitude (point data). Defaults to 'lat'.

latColumn.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Column for latitude (point data). Defaults to 'lat'.

anyOf.description: Column for longitude (point data). Defaults to 'lng'.

lngColumn.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Column for longitude (point data). Defaults to 'lng'.

anyOf.description: Column for the arc start latitude (arc layer type).

startLatColumn.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Column for the arc start latitude (arc layer type).

anyOf.description: Column for the arc start longitude (arc layer type).

startLngColumn.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Column for the arc start longitude (arc layer type).

anyOf.description: Column for the arc end latitude (arc layer type).

endLatColumn.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Column for the arc end latitude (arc layer type).

anyOf.description: Column for the arc end longitude (arc layer type).

endLngColumn.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Column for the arc end longitude (arc layer type).

anyOf.description: Show tooltip on hover. true = all properties, string[] = specific properties. Off for data rows when unset. A fused-hex overview cell always shows its hover (cell, rows, rows in window) unless this is false.

tooltip.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Show tooltip on hover. true = all properties, string[] = specific properties. Off for data rows when unset. A fused-hex overview cell always shows its hover (cell, rows, rows in window) unless this is false.

anyOf.description: Show color legend for this layer. true = auto title (the layer's name), {title} = custom title; unset or false: none. It shows fillColor's scale when fillColor is data-driven, else lineColor's when fillColor is unset and lineColor is data-driven; a single-colour fillColor shows none.

legend.description: At this level, replaces the composite's value (null unsets it here; leave it out to use the composite's). Show color legend for this layer. true = auto title (the layer's name), {title} = custom title; unset or false: none. It shows fillColor's scale when fillColor is data-driven, else lineColor's when fillColor is unset and lineColor is data-driven; a single-colour fillColor shows none.

id.description: The level's stable id: unique within the composite, letters, digits, _ and - only (e.g. "z4"). The map keeps a level's tiles and on-screen state by it, so removing or reordering levels never draws the wrong one; without it a level is known by its position in levels.

type.description: The level's layer type: any layer type but composite, read and drawn exactly as a layer of that type (fused-hex, fused-bbox, geojson, scatterplot, h3, heatmap, arc, mvt, raster, deck-geojson), fed by that type's own data keys (source, udf with tile, data, sql, tileUrl). Unset: fused-hex when the level (or the composite) names a source path or endpoint; otherwise detected from the data, as for a layer without a type.

name.description: Display name of the level in the sidebar, e.g. 'res 7'. The layer keeps the composite's name.

minZoom.description: Map zoom the level starts at (inclusive). Unset: from zoom 0. The level draws while minZoom <= map zoom < maxZoom; a tiled level's tiles start at floor(minZoom).

maxZoom.description: Map zoom the level ends at (exclusive): the next level usually starts here. Unset: no upper end. For a tiled level also the deepest zoom its tiles are requested at; past it they draw enlarged.

source.description: fused-hex and fused-bbox levels: the level's indexed dataset, as that layer's `source`: usually {path: "s3://bucket/indexed/res7/"}. path and endpoint are always the level's own (never inherited); every other key merges over the composite's `source` (options shared by every level, such as variables, loader, timeColumn, reduce, limit), a level's value replacing it and null unsetting it. `overview` is ignored (the coarser levels play that role).

anyOf.description: Inclusive start of the time window (ISO date or datetime). Required for the retrieve endpoints.

dateMin.description: Merged over the composite's source.<key> (null unsets it here). Inclusive start of the time window (ISO date or datetime). Required for the retrieve endpoints.

anyOf.description: Inclusive end of the time window (ISO date or datetime). Required for the retrieve endpoints.

dateMax.description: Merged over the composite's source.<key> (null unsets it here). Inclusive end of the time window (ISO date or datetime). Required for the retrieve endpoints.

anyOf.description: Measurement columns to fetch. Defaults to the attributes the style, tooltip and filters name, or every column when none do.

variables.description: Merged over the composite's source.<key> (null unsets it here). Measurement columns to fetch. Defaults to the attributes the style, tooltip and filters name, or every column when none do.

anyOf.description: How each hex's rows across the time window collapse to one value: latest (default) or first keep one time step; mean, min, max and sum aggregate every numeric variable and add count, date_min and date_max. Ignored while the layer's time filter on its time column holds one instant (time playback, experimental): the layer then draws that time step.

reduce.description: Merged over the composite's source.<key> (null unsets it here). How each hex's rows across the time window collapse to one value: latest (default) or first keep one time step; mean, min, max and sum aggregate every numeric variable and add count, date_min and date_max. Ignored while the layer's time filter on its time column holds one instant (time playback, experimental): the layer then draws that time step.

anyOf.description: Hourly datasets only: keep rows for this hour of the day before reducing.

hour.description: Merged over the composite's source.<key> (null unsets it here). Hourly datasets only: keep rows for this hour of the day before reducing.

anyOf.description: Column holding each row's time, used to order rows for latest/first and, with time playback (experimental), the column a time filter plays the layer's time steps on. Defaults to 'date' for the retrieve endpoints; set it for /h3/query datasets.

timeColumn.description: Merged over the composite's source.<key> (null unsets it here). Column holding each row's time, used to order rows for latest/first and, with time playback (experimental), the column a time filter plays the layer's time steps on. Defaults to 'date' for the retrieve endpoints; set it for /h3/query datasets.

anyOf.description: Server row cap per tile request (the endpoint's `limit`)

limit.description: Merged over the composite's source.<key> (null unsets it here). Server row cap per tile request (the endpoint's `limit`)

anyOf.description: Server row group cap per tile request (`max_row_groups`)

maxRowGroups.description: Merged over the composite's source.<key> (null unsets it here). Server row group cap per tile request (`max_row_groups`)

anyOf.description: Retrieve endpoints only: cell ranges the bbox cover may use (`max_ranges`). Higher values cover each tile more tightly, so fewer rows outside it are read.

maxRanges.description: Merged over the composite's source.<key> (null unsets it here). Retrieve endpoints only: cell ranges the bbox cover may use (`max_ranges`). Higher values cover each tile more tightly, so fewer rows outside it are read.

minZoom.description: The overview needs the layer's zoom floor above this (default 3). It draws at every zoom below the floor, where row tiles start.

extent.description: [west, south, east, north] the overview looks up files in, with west < east (boxes crossing the antimeridian are not supported). Row tiles are also confined to it: none are requested outside it. Cells are drawn only inside it, in the overview and in rows, by cell centre. Defaults to the whole world.

anyOf.description: Zoomed-out view below the layer's zoom floor, drawn from one request, so `overview: {}` is all it takes. Each cell is a file's H3 cell (file level) or, when the location was partitioned chunk-aligned (fused.h3.partition with chunk_res_offset) and has at most 100,000 distinct chunk cells, one row-group chunk (chunk level). The server picks the level; ERA5 and gridMET are always file level. Default at both levels: cells fill light by row count with grey outlines, not coloured by the layer's colour. Cells carry only their row counts, never column values, at either level. Hovering a cell shows it, its row count and the rows the current date window reads. Available for the ERA5 and gridMET retrieve endpoints and /h3/query. style.overview overrides the colours.

overview.description: Merged over the composite's source.<key> (null unsets it here).

anyOf.description: How each tile's row groups are read. server (the default) has the server read them and answer Parquet pages. browser reads the row groups from object storage in the browser, from a plan the server answers (/h3/query with format=browser); it needs an execution environment, and a share link without one fails. auto tries browser and falls back to server when the plan is refused or the browser loader cannot start. reader sends the query to the regional reader service (fast path for read-only Parquet pages) when the client is configured with one, and falls back to server when it is not configured or refuses the request.

loader.description: Merged over the composite's source.<key> (null unsets it here). How each tile's row groups are read. server (the default) has the server read them and answer Parquet pages. browser reads the row groups from object storage in the browser, from a plan the server answers (/h3/query with format=browser); it needs an execution environment, and a share link without one fails. auto tries browser and falls back to server when the plan is refused or the browser loader cannot start. reader sends the query to the regional reader service (fast path for read-only Parquet pages) when the client is configured with one, and falls back to server when it is not configured or refuses the request.

anyOf.description: Browser and auto loaders only: most chunks (storage range requests) the browser may fetch for one tile page. Defaults to 1000. A tile whose plan needs more is not loaded and the layer shows a warning naming the value to set here.

maxChunks.description: Merged over the composite's source.<key> (null unsets it here). Browser and auto loaders only: most chunks (storage range requests) the browser may fetch for one tile page. Defaults to 1000. A tile whose plan needs more is not loaded and the layer shows a warning naming the value to set here.

path.description: Indexed dataset location, e.g. s3://bucket/indexed/data/. Sets the endpoint to /h3/query when none is given. Needs the layer's h3Column (the location's indexed space column, 'hex' for what fused.h3.partition writes). The folder must be hex-sorted H3 parquet that fused.h3.partition wrote and fused.h3.index registered for your team (run partition, then index; pass chunk_res_offset to partition for the chunk-level overview). Not used by the retrieve endpoints, which serve a fixed dataset.

endpoint.description: Bbox query endpoint on a Fused server: a full URL or a path relative to the current server root. Supported: /retrieve/era5/daily/bbox, /retrieve/era5/hourly/bbox, /retrieve/gridmet/bbox and /h3/query. Defaults to /h3/query when path is set.

style.description: Overrides of the composite's style at this level, merged over it key by key (nested blocks such as overview one level deeper); a fillColor or lineColor given here replaces the composite's whole (e.g. a categorical fill on the finest level); null on a key unsets the composite's value here (elevationAttr: null: not extruded by attribute at this level); style: null drops the composite's style at this level.

anyOf.description: Fill color (source colour for arc, weight attr for heatmap): [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a] array, CSS string, or data-driven {type:"continuous", attr, domain?:[min,max], palette?, steps?, reverse?, nullColor?, scaleType?:"quantize"|"quantile"} | {type:"categorical", attr, colors?:{value:"#hex"}, palette?, nullColor?}. See the component description for palette names.

fillColor.description: Fill color (source colour for arc, weight attr for heatmap): [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a] array, CSS string, or data-driven {type:"continuous", attr, domain?:[min,max], palette?, steps?, reverse?, nullColor?, scaleType?:"quantize"|"quantile"} | {type:"categorical", attr, colors?:{value:"#hex"}, palette?, nullColor?}. See the component description for palette names.

anyOf.description: Stroke color (target colour for arc): [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a] array, CSS string, or the same data-driven {type:"continuous"|"categorical", attr, ...} object as fillColor. Shapes, hexagons and points draw no outline by default: setting lineColor or lineWidth turns it on.

lineColor.description: Stroke color (target colour for arc): [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a] array, CSS string, or the same data-driven {type:"continuous"|"categorical", attr, ...} object as fillColor. Shapes, hexagons and points draw no outline by default: setting lineColor or lineWidth turns it on.

anyOf.description: Stroke width in pixels. Shapes, hexagons and points draw no outline unless lineColor or lineWidth is set; 0 turns a configured outline off. Line features of a geojson layer always draw.

lineWidth.description: Stroke width in pixels. Shapes, hexagons and points draw no outline unless lineColor or lineWidth is set; 0 turns a configured outline off. Line features of a geojson layer always draw.

anyOf.description: Layer opacity 0-1
Circle radius for point features

Smallest width on screen, in pixels, of a polygon or an H3 cell. A shape keeps its real geometry until it would draw smaller, then stays this wide about its own centre (and may overlap its neighbours), so it still shows zoomed all the way out, as a stroke and a point do. Defaults to 2; 0 lets shapes shrink with the map. Not applied to extruded shapes.

minPixels.description: Smallest width on screen, in pixels, of a polygon or an H3 cell. A shape keeps its real geometry until it would draw smaller, then stays this wide about its own centre (and may overlap its neighbours), so it still shows zoomed all the way out, as a stroke and a point do. Defaults to 2; 0 lets shapes shrink with the map. Not applied to extruded shapes.

anyOf.description: H3 hex coverage 0-1 (1 = no gap, 0.8 = small gaps). Defaults to 1 for fused-hex layers, 0.9 for other hex layers.

coverage.description: H3 hex coverage 0-1 (1 = no gap, 0.8 = small gaps). Defaults to 1 for fused-hex layers, 0.9 for other hex layers.

anyOf.description: Hex layers (h3, fused-hex): numeric column that sizes each cell. Its value is mapped from coverageDomain onto a size factor in coverageRange, and the cell draws at coverage times that factor, so coverage stays the largest size. A cell with no value draws at the low end. Unset: every cell draws at coverage.

coverageAttr.description: Hex layers (h3, fused-hex): numeric column that sizes each cell. Its value is mapped from coverageDomain onto a size factor in coverageRange, and the cell draws at coverage times that factor, so coverage stays the largest size. A cell with no value draws at the low end. Unset: every cell draws at coverage.

anyOf.description: Values of coverageAttr mapped from, [low, high]: low draws at coverageRange[0], high at coverageRange[1], values between scale linearly and values outside clamp to the nearer end. Defaults to [0, 1], so set it to the column's range (e.g. [0, 500]).

coverageDomain.description: Values of coverageAttr mapped from, [low, high]: low draws at coverageRange[0], high at coverageRange[1], values between scale linearly and values outside clamp to the nearer end. Defaults to [0, 1], so set it to the column's range (e.g. [0, 500]).

anyOf.description: Size factors 0-1 that coverageDomain maps to, [low, high], each times coverage. Defaults to [0, 1]; [0.2, 1] keeps the smallest cells visible.

coverageRange.description: Size factors 0-1 that coverageDomain maps to, [low, high], each times coverage. Defaults to [0, 1]; [0.2, 1] keeps the smallest cells visible.

anyOf.description: Enable 3D extrusion (h3, deck-geojson)
Feature property to use for extrusion height

elevationAttr.description: Feature property to use for extrusion height

anyOf.description: Multiplier for extrusion height values

fused-hex only, optional: overrides how the overview cells (source.overview) draw; leave it out for the defaults, which need no setting. Defaults, at both levels: light fill by row count with #afafaf outlines at opacity 0.35, not coloured by the layer's colour. Cells carry only row counts (row_count_total, row_count_window), so a colour can only be data-driven by those; hovering a cell shows it and its row counts. Example: {fillColor: [255, 140, 0], opacity: 0.5, lineWidth: 0}. null clears a configured block (a layer switched out of fused-hex).

fillColor.description: Unset or "auto": a light fill by row_count_total at both levels, so the overview does not read as data coloured by a column. A single colour fills the cells; null draws no fill; "inherit" takes the layer's fillColor (a single colour is used as is; a data-driven one falls back to the row-count fill, since cells carry no column values); or a data-driven {type:"continuous"|"categorical", attr, ...} over the only cell properties: row_count_total (rows in the cell's files or chunk) and row_count_window (rows the current date window reads). Any other attr falls back to the row-count fill.

opacity.description: Opacity 0-1 of the overview cells, fill and outline alike. Defaults to 0.35; with fillColor "inherit" of a single colour at the chunk level, the layer's own opacity.

lineColor.description: Unset or "auto": #afafaf at both levels. A single colour outlines the cells; "inherit" takes the layer's lineColor (a data-driven one falls back to #afafaf); or a data-driven {type:"continuous"|"categorical", attr, ...} over the same cell properties as fillColor.

lineWidth.description: Overview cell stroke width in pixels. Defaults to 1 at both levels; 0 draws no outline.

stat.description: No longer used and ignored: overview cells carry no column statistics. Accepted so saved configs that set it still load.

overview.description: fused-hex only, optional: overrides how the overview cells (source.overview) draw; leave it out for the defaults, which need no setting. Defaults, at both levels: light fill by row count with #afafaf outlines at opacity 0.35, not coloured by the layer's colour. Cells carry only row counts (row_count_total, row_count_window), so a colour can only be data-driven by those; hovering a cell shows it and its row counts. Example: {fillColor: [255, 140, 0], opacity: 0.5, lineWidth: 0}. null clears a configured block (a layer switched out of fused-hex).

visible.description: Not a level key: set it on the composite, which applies it at every level. A level's is ignored (the sidebar says so).

visibleMinZoom.description: Not a level key: set it on the composite, which applies it at every level. A level's is ignored (the sidebar says so).

visibleMaxZoom.description: Not a level key: set it on the composite, which applies it at every level. A level's is ignored (the sidebar says so).

items.description: One level of a composite layer: a layer of its own (any type but composite) bound to a map zoom range (minZoom, maxZoom). It may set any layer key (type, source, udf, tile, data, sql, tileUrl, sourceLayer, filters, style, tooltip, legend, columns, ...) that differs from the composite's defaults at this level.

showControls.description: Show the zoom (+/-) buttons; the corner is controlsPosition

showScale.description: Show the scale bar; the corner is scalePosition

showCoordinates.description: Show the map centre's latitude, longitude and zoom (a click copies them); the corner is coordinatesPosition. In a shared corner it sits under the scale bar.

showSearch.description: Show a geocoder search (in the corner searchPosition sets, top-right by default), which accepts place names, "lat, lng" pairs, H3 cell IDs.

showBasemapSwitcher.description: Offer the dark/light/satellite basemap choice: the sidebar's Base map tab, or a floating toggle when showSidebar is false

showLegend.description: Show color legend for layers with data-driven colors

showTooltip.description: Map-level switch for the hover and pinned (click) tooltip cards: false turns them off for every layer, true leaves each layer's own `tooltip` setting in charge. A `$param` reference (e.g. "$show_tips") is read live, so a page can turn the cards on and off with fused.params.set("show_tips", false) without reloading the map; turning them off closes any open card. The sidebar Tooltip switch writes the bound param (off: false, on: true), so the page can follow with fused.params.onChange. hoverParam, clickParam and selectParam keep working while the cards are off.

anyOf.description: A canvas parameter reference such as `$show_tips`, read live: tooltips are off while it holds false, "false", 0, "0" or "", and on for any other value or while it has none

showLayerPanel.description: Show the floating layer panel for toggling visibility and opacity when showSidebar is false (the sidebar's layer list covers this otherwise)

showSidebar.description: Show the sidebar toggle for editing layer style, filters and SQL at runtime. On your own canvas the edits are written into this config as you make them (undo with Cmd/Ctrl+Z in the sidebar or the code editor); elsewhere they are runtime overrides you can copy into the config.

searchPosition.description: Corner the place search (showSearch) sits in; in a bottom corner its results open above the box.

basemapSwitcherPosition.description: Corner the floating basemap toggle (showBasemapSwitcher) sits in. Only used when showSidebar is false: with the sidebar on, the basemap choice is its Base map tab.

layerPanelPosition.description: Corner the floating layer panel (showLayerPanel) sits in. Only used when showSidebar is false: with the sidebar on, its layer list covers this.

controlsPosition.description: Corner the zoom buttons (showControls) sit in. The scale bar (scalePosition) and the coordinates readout (coordinatesPosition) follow it unless they set their own corner, so setting only this moves all three. Controls sharing a corner stack away from it in a fixed order: zoom buttons, scale bar, coordinates readout; then, past those, the other floating controls placed there by the *Position props (sidebar toggle, search, layer panel, basemap switcher, legend, reset view, clear selection). Their panels open towards the middle of the map. The sidebar toggle, reset view and clear selection buttons always sit top-left.

scalePosition.description: Corner the scale bar (showScale) sits in. Unset: the same corner as the zoom buttons (controlsPosition).

coordinatesPosition.description: Corner the coordinates readout (showCoordinates) sits in. Unset: the same corner as the zoom buttons (controlsPosition).

param.description: Canvas parameter name to sync viewport bounds [west, south, east, north]

autoSendDebounceMs.description: Debounce ms for auto-send (0 = send on every move)

clickParam.description: Canvas parameter that receives the properties of the last clicked feature

hoverParam.description: Canvas parameter that receives the properties of the feature under the cursor, in the same shape as clickParam (only the layer's tooltip fields when it lists them). Sent at most once per animation frame and only when the hovered feature changes; a new feature is not sent while the map is dragged. Cleared (removed, like fused.params.set(name, null)) when the cursor leaves every feature. Session state: not saved with the canvas.

selectParam.description: Canvas parameter that receives the current selection: shift+drag draws a box (the map dims outside it), shift+click toggles one feature, Escape or a plain click on the map clears. Value: { layer, key, ids, count, bbox, mode, truncated }. Session state: not saved with the canvas. bbox is the [west, south, east, north] envelope of the drawn box (null for click selections) and is the selection for a box: filter rows by it. ids are the `selectKey` values of every feature drawn in the box, with no cap; truncated is always false. Another widget or an HTML page can write it too: null or an empty selection ({ mode: "none" } or { ids: [], bbox: null }) clears the outline and dimming, and { bbox: [west, south, east, north] } draws that box (its ids are not re-picked; west must be less than east). Only nodes wired to the map by an edge in either direction (or the page it is embedded in) are heard, and only writes made while the map is mounted. Ids without a bbox do not change what the map shows.

sourceParam.description: Canvas parameter that signals when a layer's `{{layer_id}}` rows change, so a page can re-query instead of polling. Value: { [sourceName]: { version, loading, rows, error, tiles?, level?, band? } }, one entry per published source: each layer id, and for a composite layer both `id` and `id_drawn`. Re-run fused.query when version changes (compare with !==, not >). version is 0 while the source has no rows, loading is true while newer rows are built, rows is the row count when known (else null), error is the last build error. A tiled layer's view source (fused-hex, h3 udf tiles) and a composite's two sources add tiles: the number of tiles in view the rows come from. A composite's two sources add level (index in `levels` of the level on screen, null when none) and band ([minZoom, maxZoom] of that level, null for an open end). tiles, level and band change together with the rows they describe. Session state: not saved with the canvas.

playbackParam.description: Canvas parameter that receives the time playback bar's position, so a page can follow it while it plays (a chart marker, a date label). Value while the bar is open: { layer, attr, min, max, cursor, playing, mode }. min and max are the time window the map draws, as ISO text, live while playing or while a handle is dragged (written at most 10 times a second, the last position always); cursor is Point mode's cursor (ISO) or null; playing is true while the bar plays; mode is the bar's mode (auto, window, point, cumulative). Null when the bar is closed. Read-only: to move the window, write the time filter's bound parameters. Session state: not saved with the canvas.

selectKey.description: Feature property published as each selected feature's id in selectParam. Defaults to the cell column on hex layers, else `id`.

stateParam.description: Canvas parameter that mirrors the map's runtime state (camera, layer type, style, filters, SQL overrides) so other widgets can read it. It is saved with the canvas and restored on reload (the camera only when the config sets no centerLng/centerLat). On your own canvas layer edits are written into this config as you make them, so the parameter mostly carries the camera. The camera is `view`: { centerLng, centerLat, zoom, bearing, pitch, width, height }, written when a pan, zoom, rotate or tilt gesture ends (not during it). zoom is exact (6 decimals, Web Mercator with 512 px tiles), bearing and pitch are degrees, and width and height are the map canvas size in CSS pixels at that moment, so a page can project lng/lat to pixels; width and height are ignored when the camera is restored. A page can move the camera by writing `view` while the map is open: it jumps there, or flies there when the view carries `transition` (duration in ms, e.g. { centerLng, centerLat, zoom, transition: 1500 }). `transition` is used once: when the flight starts the map writes the view back without it, and a view restored on reload always jumps.

style.description: Inline CSS styles as a plain CSS string
